canonical_definition:
What it is. Papers most commonly treat MMT-Bench as a multimodal benchmark for evaluating large vision-language models on multitask performance. The most specific description says it "covers 162 concrete sub-tasks" drawn from existing datasets, is primarily focused on perception, uses a multiple-choice question format, and enables in-depth analysis through its "taskonomy" and diverse input forms (MEGA-Bench: Scaling Multimodal Evaluation to over 500 Real-World Tasks). Another paper places it among widely-adopted VLM benchmarks and also refers to it as a visual question answering benchmark.

What it is claimed to measure. Across the papers, MMT-Bench is used to measure 1 behavioral indicator, Visual question answering, and no constructs are linked to it. The claims therefore concentrate on a single behavioral use, with a paper presenting MMT-Bench as a visual question answering benchmark.

Space of uses. No measurement instrument is linked to it. In use, papers report results on MMT-Bench alongside other widely-adopted VLM benchmarks, and a paper positions it within a comparative table of visual question answering benchmarks for leading methods.
